propositions: A model class configured with provider='bedrock' and a canonical versioned Bedrock model id (e.g. 'us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0') has its configured provider silently discarded because the model id contains a colon
The _resolve_target function incorrectly treats any model string containing a colon as already provider-qualified, causing it to return the bare model string without prefixing the configured provider

An unqualified versioned Bedrock model id is later parsed by infer_provider as 'provider:model' on the first colon, resulting in the model id being split incorrectly and downstream provider factory rejection

Two independent implementations of the qualified/unqualified decision (one colon scan in _resolve_target, another in infer_provider) can drift apart and both fail identically for versioned Bedrock ids
An explicitly configured provider must be checked and honored first, before any model string is scanned, so punctuation in a model id cannot overrule or discard it
A conflicting configured-provider and inline-qualifier pair must raise an error rather than silently picking a winner
